visible.summary:
Cajamarca has no documented trans-specific regional law, ordinance or incident series; the binding framework is national. In February 2025 the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved bills 6506 and 8457 barring trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than their birth sex — exceptions only for custody, medical care and accompanying under-12s, the elderly or disabled — and banning ambiguous signage. On 2 April 2025 the plenary approved the fused text without a second vote; a university human-rights institute analyzed Article 5.1 as a direct violation of constitutional equality and inter-American non-discrimination standards, while activists note enforcement falls to individual security staff judging IDs.

Violence evidence is national: the university TLGBI observatory counted 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023 (30 victims trans women; killings marked by extreme cruelty, and a 2023 gang extortion-murder of a trans sex worker in the capital). The national machinery applies fully to Cajamarca.
visible.tangentialFactors: Community-justice assemblies (rondas campesinas) hold dispute-resolution authority in parts of this department, and the constitution permits community justice within human-rights limits: a complaint — including one over gender expression — may be settled by a campesino assembly rather than in court. No trans-specific case documented; recorded as a structural caveat from the country dossier.

sources.claim: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): the congressional Comision de Mujer y Familia approved by unanimity a dictamen merging bills 6506 and 8457 (sponsored by Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Munante) that would prohibit any person from entering public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite to their birth sex, with narrow exceptions (custody, and cases where required, including accompanying minors, the elderly or people with disabilities), and would oblige venues not to post ambiguous restroom signs; the article notes the text still needed plenary backing and reports the trigger as the July 2023 complaint over gendered restroom labels at Lima's Jorge Chavez international airport. Activist Gianna Camacho is quoted arguing the measure is discriminatory and that enforcement would rest on security staff checking the DNI to decide whether a woman entering a women's restroom is trans or cisgender. This is the national framework this department is scored against; the article contains no Cajamarca-specific content.

IDEHPUCP legal analysis (15 April 2025, Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte): on Wednesday 2 April 2025 the plenary of Congress approved and waived a second vote on the dictamen of the 'Ley que fortalece el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los ninos y adolescentes', whose Article 5.1 prohibits persons from entering or using public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than their birth sex. The institute reads Article 5 as a direct breach of equality and non-discrimination (Article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and Article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights), resting on the stereotype that trans people are more prone to enter restrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors, and recalls documented cases of trans people barred from public restrooms - including SPC-INDECOPI Resolution 0735-2022 dismissing a trans woman's discrimination complaint against SmartFit, where the company grounded bathroom assignment on the sex recorded in the DNI - and the fact that gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive. This is the national framework this department is scored against; the article contains no Cajamarca-specific content.

Agencia Presentes (22 July 2024), drawing on the annual report of the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI of Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia: Peru recorded 54 assassinations of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases in 2020-2023, the homicide victims being 30 trans women, 23 gay men and one lesbian; 19 killings occurred in 2023 alone (12 of them trans women), and killers were not identified in 26 of the 54 homicides (13 of 19 in 2023). The piece recounts the February 2023 murder of trans sex worker Rubi Torres Silvano (31), kidnapped from central Lima by a 'Los Gallegos' extortion gang and killed in Carabayllo with some 30 gunshots (Priscila Aguado Huatuco, 30, was shot days earlier), with two killers arrested in March 2023, and notes the state has not incorporated sexual orientation or gender identity into its crime-registration systems, so hate crimes cannot be prosecuted as such. This is the national violence baseline this department is scored against; the article contains no Cajamarca-specific content.

visible.summary:
This province has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; what a trans visitor here stands under is the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked draft omnibus justice package from October 2025 (the '11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people across Turkiye - Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades - and it contains no province-specific provisions. The LGBTI+ association Kaos GL reported that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as state policy under a 'Year of the Family' banner, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions creating a climate encouraging rights violations.

Because the surviving record is entirely national-level and carries no provincial breakdown, neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged.
visible.tangentialFactors: The draft 11th Judicial Package's penalties for symbolic same-sex ceremonies (up to 4 years) and the nationwide 2025 'Year of the Family' hostility campaign shape police posture toward gender-nonconforming people here as in every other province, even before the amendments are enacted.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 Oct 2025) on the leaked '11th Judicial Package' draft omnibus law: would amend the Turkish penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', criminalise taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (penalties up to 4 years in prison), raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility, and punish health professionals who perform such care - HRW calls it one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades, and 15 Turkish LGBT groups plus the Turkish Medical Association oppose the draft.

Kaos GL report launch on the 2025 report 'A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy': documents that anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as explicit state policy, with senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate that encouraged human-rights violations, and regulatory/supervisory bodies systematically restricting freedom of expression and artistic freedom; findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the launch.
